usability.observation: Does the dialog clearly say HOW MANY exercises exceeded target and that ONLY weight is updated (not sets/reps)?

usability.name: Running page hidden by default
usability.heuristic: Nielsen #7: Flexibility and efficiency of use
usability.observation: Power users who want Running must discover the toggle in Settings. Is there any hint in the nav or onboarding?

usability.name: Theme selector: Light/Dark/Auto replacing single Dark Mode toggle
usability.heuristic: Match between system and real world
usability.observation: 'Auto' assumes the user already knows it means 'follow OS appearance' — a non-technical user may be unsure what it does or be confused later when appearance changes without an in-app explanation.

usability.name: History nested filtering: domain tab -> sub-filter -> period filter
usability.heuristic: Flexibility and efficiency of use vs. Aesthetic and minimalist design
usability.observation: Two levels of nested filtering (Strength/Cardio tab, then Running/Elliptical/All, then Month/Year/All) is powerful for precise review but may need several taps for a casual user who just wants to glance at recent history, and the sub-filter's scoping to Cardio only may not be obvious.

usability.name: Login screen: Google sign-in button visual weight vs. primary email/password flow
usability.heuristic: Aesthetic and minimalist design / Consistency and standards
usability.observation: Depending on placement/styling, the Google button could either be a helpful shortcut or visually compete with the primary email/password flow, especially for users who registered with email/password.

usability.name: Login error message: generic 'Invalid email or password' for both wrong-password and unknown-email cases
usability.heuristic: Help users recognize, diagnose, and recover from errors
usability.observation: The identical message for both cases (an intentional anti-enumeration tradeoff) gives no hint about which field to check, so a user with a mistyped email may keep retrying the same correct password rather than fixing the email.

usability.name: Settings 'Show Cardio Page' checkbox renamed from 'Show Running Page', swaps nav tab to 'Cardio'
usability.heuristic: Match between system and real world
usability.observation: A user who mentally maps this toggle to 'running' may not immediately recognize 'Cardio' as the same feature, and the destination page's running/elliptical-specific language may feel inconsistent with the broader 'Cardio' label.

bugs.title: Settings plan-edit panel open/close transition causes large layout shift (CLS)
bugs.detail: Measured cumulative layout shift ~934-939 on both Edit Strength Plan and Edit Cardio Workout Plan panel transitions, consistently, on both panels. No hard app-defined budget exists, but this is a large, real, repeatable shift.

bugs.title: No ARIA state exposure anywhere in the app for custom toggle/tab-like controls
bugs.detail: Theme selector and History Strength/Cardio domain switcher expose active state via CSS .active class only -- zero aria-pressed/aria-selected/role=tab in the entire app (confirmed by direct source grep). Screen reader users cannot perceive which option is selected.

bugs.title: axe-core not installed in project despite qa-state.json tagging some cases tool: axe-core
bugs.detail: Not a product bug -- a QA-tooling gap. These ran as manual DOM/ARIA checks instead.

bugs.title: TC-SEC-015 cross-account cardio data isolation: CONFIRMED SAFE
bugs.detail: Test setup had 3 stacked bugs (checkbox needed label-click not .check(), #mainGearBtn unreachable from History section during cleanup, missing logout import) -- fixed all 3 and re-ran. Test now passes for real: cardio history stats ARE correctly scoped per-account, no data leakage between test@gmail.com and testeitan@gmail.com. This was previously blocked_by_verification, now resolved.

bugs.title: Cardio streak number fails WCAG AA contrast in dark mode
bugs.detail: Measured contrast ratio 2.81:1 for .run-streak-num text against its background in dark mode -- well below the 4.5:1 WCAG AA minimum for body text. Confirmed only after fixing an unrelated test-navigation bug that was masking this assertion from ever running. Reproduced consistently on BOTH chromium and mobile-android in the final verification pass.

bugs.title: History Strength/Cardio domain tab switcher overflows 375px viewport by ~11px
bugs.detail: Rightmost edge of the tab pair measured at x=387 against a 375px viewport (376px incl. 1px tolerance). Minor horizontal overflow, not reproduced as a page-body scroll issue elsewhere in this run. Final verification: flaky (failed once, passed on retry) -- likely a borderline/marginal overflow (~11px), not a solid reproducible one. Downgraded from medium.
